The 1860 census record has three extracted assertions, all under the `child_2` role: a_008 (name — Patrick Flynn), a_009 (birth — age 15, Ireland), and a_010 (relationship — listed in Thomas Flynn's household, consistent with son).

Neither the name assertion nor the birth assertion has any `person_evidence` entry at all. Only the relationship assertion (a_010) was linked. These two assertions belong to the same `child_2` persona as a_010 and should link to the same person — Patrick Flynn (I1). **Gap 2 — a_010 is linked to Patrick Flynn (I1) only; Thomas Flynn (I2) is missing.**

No warnings on any of the four persons. Everything is clean.

---

The 1860 census lists Joseph Pratt as head of household (born in England, around 1822), alongside Ann Pratt (around 1825), Sarah Pratt (around 1847), and a younger Joseph Pratt (around 1850), all born in England, all living in Salt Lake County, Utah Territory. The 1880 census shows the same couple — now older — still in Salt Lake County, with their son Joseph still in the household. Every name, birth year, birthplace, and family position in both records fits the known family in the tree, and the family's move from England to Utah is well explained: the Utah Emigration and Immigration research guide specifically notes that many immigrants from Great Britain sailed on chartered ships from Liverpool, England, to reach Utah — a well-documented corridor for this era and this county. The same-person scoring returned 0.78 for every pairing, solidly in the strong range, and no birth year, birthplace, or relationship conflict was found for any member. All twenty assertions from the two censuses were linked with high confidence: Joseph (head) very confidently to the subject of the research, Ann very confidently to his wife, Sarah very confidently to their daughter, and the younger Joseph very confidently to their son. The census facts — birth years, birthplaces, residences, and the spousal and child relationships stated in the 1880 record — have been written onto each person's tree entry.

One detail to follow up on: Sarah Pratt, who appears as a thirteen-year-old in 1860, is entirely absent from the 1880 household. She may have died in the intervening twenty years, married and moved into a separate household, or been enumerated elsewhere; the records in hand cannot settle which. Searching for a marriage record, a death record, or a later census entry for Sarah Pratt in Utah would answer this.

dimensions.name: Correctness
dimensions.rationale: All 22 person_evidence links are factually correct. Names, ages, birth years, and birthplaces match across both censuses and align with tree persons. The confidence tier of 'probable' is correctly applied across all links per the decided rule: the transatlantic move from Horsham, Sussex to Maury County, Tennessee is unexplained by any documentary bridge or corridor in the project, capping the link at probable despite strong non-location identifiers (0.78 score). The rationales consistently name the geographic gap (6804 km, no corridor from England in the 1860s per wiki_read, no passenger list or naturalization in project). Tree facts were enriched with residence assertions from both censuses with proper source refs (S10, S11). No fabricated material or unsupported claims.

dimensions.name: Completeness
dimensions.rationale: All 20 assertions from both census records (11 from 1870, 9 from 1880) were linked to the correct tree persons. The 1870 household (William, Mary, James, Ellen, George) and 1880 household (William, Mary, George) were fully processed. Both relationship assertions (wife, son) in the 1880 census were linked to both parties as required. The absence of James and Ellen in 1880 was noted as an open identity question. Tree.gedcomx.json was enriched with residence facts for all five persons. No required work was omitted.

dimensions.name: Tool Arguments
dimensions.rationale: All 32 MCP tool calls passed correct arguments. same_person calls correctly paired each assertion with its tree person (e.g., a_001 with I1, a_003 with I2). place_search calls for 'Maury County, Tennessee' and 'Horsham, Sussex, England' matched expected substring patterns. place_distance correctly measured Horsham, Sussex, England to Maury, Tennessee (6804 km returned). wiki_read correctly targeted Tennessee_Emigration_and_Immigration. research_append and materialize_facts calls were well-formed with proper person IDs and record roles. No fixture_not_found errors. No critical identifiers were wrong.

dimensions.name: Confidence calibration
dimensions.rationale: All 22 links are scored 'probable', which is correct per the decided rule. The 0.78 match_score from same_person indicates strong correlation on name, age, birth year, birthplace, and household composition — all non-location identifiers. However, the transatlantic move (Horsham to Maury County, 6804 km) is unexplained: no passenger list, naturalization, or emigration record in the project; Tennessee_Emigration_and_Immigration wiki page names no qualifying corridor from Sussex in the 1860s. This gap prevents 'confident' but does not contradict the link, so 'probable' is the correct tier. No link was scored 'confident' despite the strong score, and no link was scored 'speculative' (which would over-apply the rule). The rationale consistently names the geographic gap.

dimensions.name: Rationale quality
dimensions.rationale: Each rationale cites specific matching attributes: name (exact match 'William Weller', 'Mary Weller', etc.), age (record gives ~1825 for William in 1870, tree person ~1825, gap 0 years), birth year consistency, birthplace (England), household position (head, wife, son, household members), and family context (children's names and ages align). Rationales address the geographic gap explicitly: 'Maury County, Tennessee, 1870 vs. nearest attested residence England (pre-run): outside 6804 km; Tennessee emigration page names no qualifying arrival corridor from England in the 1860s era; no documentary bridge in project.' Competing candidates are implicitly ruled out by the exact name and age matches in a small household. Rationales are substantive, not generic.

dimensions.name: Multi-person awareness
dimensions.rationale: Both relationship assertions in the 1880 census (a_019 'Wife of William Weller' and a_020 'Son of William Weller') were linked to both parties. a_019 generated pe_017 (I2 as primary party) and pe_021 (I1 as related party). a_020 generated pe_020 (I5 as primary party) and pe_022 (I1 as related party). Each relationship is represented by two person_evidence entries, one for each person in the relationship. The skill correctly recognized that a relationship assertion bears on both parties and created links for both.

dimensions.name: Person minting and connecting edges
dimensions.rationale: No new persons needed to be minted: all five census personas (CP1–CP5 in 1870, DP1–DP3 in 1880) matched existing tree persons (I1–I5). materialize_facts was called to enrich the existing persons with residence facts from both censuses, with proper source refs (S10 for 1870, S11 for 1880). The tool returned factsAdded and factsEnriched counts confirming facts were written. No edges needed to be written via tree_edit add_relationship because the scenario is two independent census records (non-household-linking records in the genealogical sense — they do not co-enumerate a household across time). The skill correctly did not attempt to write edges. All persons remain non-null and properly sourced.

dimensions.name: Score discipline
dimensions.rationale: same_person was invoked for every assertion paired with a tree candidate (26 calls total across all assertions and relationship parties). Each call returned a score of 0.78 (strong band, confidence 4). The score was recorded in match_score and informed the confidence decision: the high score supported the 'probable' tier (not overridden by it), but did not elevate to 'confident' because the geographic gap capped it. The score was treated as input that informs correlation analysis, not as the verdict. For relationship assertions, the second party (head) was scored via recordRole parameter (e.g., a_019 with I1 recordRole='head'), correctly avoiding reuse of the first party's persona. No score was invoked where no tree candidate existed (all five persons were pre-existing). The tool was used correctly and the score was respected without overriding the geographic constraint.
